vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: tickerdb
Version: 0.1.95

The tickerdb skill bundle is a legitimate integration for a financial market data service. It provides structured instructions for an AI agent to handle authentication via email verification, manage a server-side watchlist, and perform market analysis using the api.tickerdb.com endpoints. The inclusion of slash commands and cron job templates aligns with the intended functionality of the OpenClaw platform, and no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or harmful prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: The skill's requests and runtime instructions are consistent with a market-data API integration: it only needs a TICKERDB API key and calls api.tickerdb.com endpoints for onboarding and per-ticker queries.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (market context for agents) align with the declared requirement (TICKERDB_KEY) and the SKILL.md, which documents calls to api.tickerdb.com for summaries and onboarding. No unrelated services, binaries, or config paths are requested.

dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to perform only onboarding (email + code exchange) and per-ticker GET requests to the TickerDB API. It does not instruct reading local files, other env vars, or sending data to third-party endpoints outside tickerdb.com.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files — instruction-only. Nothing is downloaded or written by the skill itself beyond relying on the platform's normal persistence for storing the API key if the user consents.

dimensions.detail: Only a single credential (TICKERDB_KEY) is required and documented as a bearer token for the API. No unrelated secrets or high-privilege environment access are requested.

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: it will call api.tickerdb.com and needs your TICKERDB_KEY. Before installing, verify you trust tickerdb.com (review privacy, pricing, and what data they retain). When you authenticate, you'll provide an email and a verification code; only save the returned API key if you understand and consent to the platform persisting it. Limit the key's scope if possible and be prepared to rotate/revoke it if you stop using the skill. If you need stronger isolation, avoid saving the key and paste it only for ephemeral use.
